channel.title: Chevrolet recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Buick and Chevrolet Rearview Camera May Show Blank Image
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Buick Envista, Buick Encore GX, Chevrolet Trailblazer, and Chevrolet Trax vehicles because the rearview camera screen may display a distorted or blank image instead of showing what's behind the vehicle clearly.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado, GMC Sierra 2500 tire pressure label wrong
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Chevrolet Silverado 2500 and GMC Sierra 2500 trucks built with the enhanced towing option and the 20-inch accessory tire and wheel package. The label that lists tire pressures may show the wrong pressure for the rear tires. Going by it can leave those tires underinflated, and it can also keep the truck's tire pressure monitoring system from showing a low tire pressure warning. Dealers will inspect, update software, add a corrected label overlay, and set the tires to the right pressure as needed, free of charge.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado, GMC Sierra Roof Air Bag Inflator Risk
item.description: The end cap on the roof rail air bag inflator, on the left or right side, may come loose, or the inflator itself may rupture. This can let compressed gas escape and send the end cap or inflator pieces into the vehicle.

item.title: Cadillac, Chevrolet, GMC SUVs Have Wrong Wheel Bolts
item.description: Some 2025 and 2026 Cadillac Escalade, Escalade ESV, Chevrolet Tahoe, GMC Yukon, and Yukon XL vehicles with 24-inch wheels may have the wrong bolts installed on the left and right front wheel hubs. Over time, these incorrect bolts can loosen or become deformed. This affects how securely the front wheels are held onto the vehicle, since the bolts holding them in place are not the correct type for these hubs.

item.title: Chevrolet Tahoe, GMC Yukon Wheels Can Lock Up
item.description: A part is missing from the transfer case, which is the part of your vehicle that sends power to the front and rear wheels. Because this part is missing, the front wheels, the rear wheels, or both can suddenly lock up while you are driving. This can happen with no warning to you as the driver, at any time you are on the road.

item.title: Chevrolet Malibu rearview camera may show blank or distorted image
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Chevrolet Malibu vehicles because the rearview camera screen may show a distorted picture or no picture at all. A dealer will inspect the camera and, if needed, replace it at no cost to the owner. General Motors mailed notification letters to owners, and Chevrolet has a customer service line for owners who have questions. Owners can also look up whether their own vehicle is covered by this recall using their vehicle identification number.

item.title: Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra Roof Air Bag Defect
item.description: Certain Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra crew cab trucks have a roof rail air bag whose inflator may have a problem. The end cap on the left or right side inflator could detach, or the inflator itself could rupture. If that happens, it can release compressed gas and send the end cap or pieces of the inflator into the vehicle.

item.title: Silverado and Sierra 3500 Fuel Pump May Stall Engine
item.description: On these trucks, which are built with gasoline engines and have two separate fuel tanks, the rear tank's fuel pump may not transfer an adequate amount of fuel over to the front tank. Because of this, the front tank may not receive enough fuel to keep the engine running properly, and the engine can stall while the truck is being driven.

item.title: GM vehicles may be missing the electronic owner's manual
item.description: General Motors is recalling a wide range of Cadillac, Chevrolet, GMC and Buick vehicles, including the Escalade IQ and IQL, OPTIQ, Colorado, Equinox EV, Silverado 3500, Canyon and Sierra 3500. During production, the radio may not have been set to the correct status to download the electronic owner's manual, so the manual is not there for the owner to use. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard covering occupant protection.

item.title: Cadillac, Chevrolet, GMC SUVs Rear Wheel Lockup
item.description: On these Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC SUVs equipped with a 10-speed automatic transmission, the transmission control valve may fail. If the valve fails, it can cause the rear wheels to lock up while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado, GMC Sierra Transmission Wheel Lockup Risk
item.description: Certain Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra trucks may not have been fully fixed by an earlier recall that addressed this same transmission problem. In these trucks, the transmission control valve can fail. When that happens, the rear wheels may lock up suddenly while the truck is being driven.

item.title: Chevrolet Blazer EV Parking Brake Wiring Fault
item.description: In some Chevrolet Blazer EV vehicles that were previously repaired under an earlier recall, the rear parking brake wiring harness may become damaged or corroded. This can cause the parking brake to activate on its own or to stop working.

item.title: Chevrolet Equinox EV Pedestrian Alert Sound Issue
item.description: These electric Equinox vehicles are supposed to make a sound that gets noticeably louder when the vehicle starts moving from a stop, so pedestrians can tell it's no longer parked. In some vehicles, the sound doesn't change enough in volume between being stopped and moving at low speed, so it doesn't meet the federal safety standard for the noise electric and hybrid vehicles must make.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado Trucks Missing Owner's Manual
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain 2026 Chevrolet Silverado 1500, 2500 and 3500 trucks that may not have been given an owner's manual when they were built. The manual contains information owners need to safely use and operate the vehicle. Without it, an owner may not have that information, which increases the risk of injury in a crash.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado 4500 Brake Wiring Repair Redo
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Chevrolet Silverado 4500HD, 5500HD, and 6500HD trucks. These vehicles already had a brake wiring fix done under an earlier recall, but the wire harness used in that repair was installed without protective tape. Without this tape, the wires can become damaged. Because of this, GM says these trucks need to have that earlier repair redone, with the tape properly added before the wiring harness is put back in place.

item.title: Cadillac Optiq, Equinox EV Tire Tread Detachment
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain 2025-2026 Cadillac Optiq and 2025-2026 Chevrolet Equinox EV vehicles that are equipped with 21-inch Continental all-season tires. On some of these vehicles, part of the tire's tread, or the entire tread, may separate from the tire while the vehicle is being driven. This is known as tread detachment and can affect one or more of the vehicle's tires.

item.title: Nissan NV200, Chevrolet City Express Fuel Pump Fuse Risk
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain NV200 vans, NV200 taxis, and Chevrolet City Express vans. In these vehicles, a wiring harness for a sensor near the fuel tank may have been routed incorrectly. Because of this, the wires can become damaged and cause a short circuit. That short circuit can blow the fuse that powers the fuel pump, cutting off power to it.

item.title: Equinox EV Pedestrian Alert Sound Too Quiet
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Chevrolet Equinox EV vehicles because the pedestrian alert sound system may not produce enough of a change in volume between when the vehicle is stopped and when it is moving at low speeds. This sound is meant to let people outside the vehicle know it is there. Because the volume does not change enough, the vehicle does not meet the federal minimum sound requirements for hybrid and electric vehicles.

item.title: Cadillac, Chevy, GMC SUVs Have Wrong Fuel Tank
item.description: Certain Cadillac Escalade, Chevrolet Tahoe, and GMC Yukon vehicles with a 6-cylinder diesel engine may have had their original fuel tank replaced with the wrong one. If that happened, fuel could leak out of the tank if the vehicle is involved in a rollover crash.

item.title: Chevrolet Corvette Fuel Leak Fire Risk
item.description: Some Chevrolet Corvette vehicles with a left-side radiator and fan combination may allow extra fuel to spill into the fuel-filler pocket area during refueling. That spilled fuel could then leak out and land on a nearby ignition source, such as a hot engine or exhaust part.

item.title: Silverado, Sierra Roof Airbag Inflator May Rupture
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra pickup trucks. These trucks have airbags built into the roof rail, above the doors. On the left or right side, the metal end cap on the airbag inflator may come loose and detach, or the inflator itself may crack open, or rupture.

item.title: Chevrolet Blazer EV Parking Brake Wiring Problem
item.description: The wiring that controls the rear parking brake on these vehicles can become damaged or corroded over time. If this happens, the parking brake may switch on by itself while you are driving, even though you didn't touch it. The same wiring problem can also cause the parking brake to stop working altogether once the vehicle is parked, so it may not hold the vehicle in place. Either way, the parking brake isn't functioning the way it's supposed to.

item.title: Chevrolet Medium Duty Silverado Brake Sensor Fire Risk
item.description: Certain Chevrolet Silverado 4500HD, 5500HD, and 6500HD medium duty trucks have a brake pressure sensor assembly that may leak brake fluid into the nearby brake pressure switch. This leak can cause an electrical short circuit, which can overheat the circuit and increase the risk of a fire, whether the truck is being driven or is parked.

item.title: GM Trucks and SUVs Engine May Fail
item.description: Certain Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC trucks and SUVs with a 6.2L V8 gas engine may have manufacturing defects in the connecting rod and/or crankshaft. These defects can damage the engine and cause it to fail.

item.title: GM Cars: Electric Power Steering Assist May Fail
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain 2016-2018 Cadillac CTS, 2017-2018 Cadillac ATS, Chevrolet Camaro, and Chevrolet Corvette vehicles. The electric power steering assist may fail while the vehicle is being driven. This power steering system normally helps reduce the effort needed to turn the steering wheel, and this recall covers vehicles where that assist can stop working.

item.title: Cadillac and Camaro Transmission May Lock Wheels
item.description: The 10-speed transmission in these vehicles may become damaged internally, and that damage can cause the wheels to lock up while driving. A wheel locking up while driving increases the risk of a crash. Dealers will install new monitoring software in the transmission's computer to address the problem, free of charge.

item.title: Chevrolet Equinox EV Cruise Control May Not Brake
item.description: On certain 2025 Chevrolet Equinox EV all-wheel drive electric vehicles, the adaptive cruise control system may not apply the brakes the way it is supposed to when needed. This happens because of incorrect software installed in the module that controls the vehicle's brake system. As a result, the brakes may not engage automatically as the driver expects when the adaptive cruise control feature is being used.

item.title: Chevy Silverado EV, GMC Sierra EV Seat Belt Bolt
item.description: On some of these electric pickup trucks, the bolt that holds the rear center seat belt to the seat structure may not have been tightened enough during assembly. Because of this, the bolt securing that seat belt to the seat frame could be looser than it is supposed to be, instead of being properly fastened in place. That means the seat belt itself may not stay as firmly attached as it should.

item.title: Silverado EV Pedestrian Alert Sound May Be Too Quiet
item.description: On some Chevrolet Silverado EV work trucks, the pedestrian alert sound system may not produce sound loud enough.

item.title: Chevy Equinox EV Pedestrian Warning Sound Too Quiet
item.description: On some 2025 Chevrolet Equinox EV vehicles, the software that controls the pedestrian alert sound system may be incorrect, and the vehicle may not produce the alert sound at a loud enough volume. This system is meant to make noise so that people walking nearby can hear the vehicle approaching. Dealers will update the body control module software to fix the issue, free of charge.

item.title: Silverado and Sierra Tailgates May Unlatch
item.description: Some Chevrolet Silverado HD and GMC Sierra HD trucks have a power tailgate release switch that can short out if water gets into it. This can cause the tailgate to unlock itself even while the truck is parked. If that happens while you're driving, the tailgate could swing open and any cargo in the bed could fall out, creating a hazard for other drivers.

item.title: Chevrolet Express Transmission Software May Cause Unintended Movement
item.description: GM is recalling certain Chevrolet Express and GMC Savana vans because of incorrect software in the transmission control module. This software problem can cause harsh shifting, reduced power, the vehicle slowing down on its own, the rear wheels locking up, or the vehicle moving in a direction the driver did not intend.

item.title: Chevrolet Bolt EV/EUV: Battery Fire Risk When Fully Charged
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Chevrolet Bolt EV and Bolt EUV vehicles that were previously repaired under an earlier recall. The installation of advanced diagnostic software on these vehicles may have failed. Because of this, the high voltage battery could catch fire when it is charged to full or nearly full capacity. A battery fire increases the risk of injury to occupants.

item.title: Diesel GM trucks, SUVs risk rear wheel lock-up
item.description: On certain diesel Chevrolet, GMC and Cadillac trucks and SUVs, the transmission control valve may fail. If it fails, the rear wheels can lock up while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Chevrolet Silverado, GMC Sierra Side Airbag Inflator Defect
item.description: Certain Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra crew cab trucks have a problem with the roof-rail side curtain airbag. The end cap on the left or right side inflator may separate from the inflator, or the inflator's sidewall may split open. If this happens, compressed gas inside can escape suddenly, sending the end cap or other pieces flying into the vehicle.

item.title: Chevrolet Blazer, Equinox EV Door Striker Failure
item.description: The door strikers on your vehicle were not properly heat-treated, which can cause them to break. If a door striker breaks, the door it's attached to can open unexpectedly, which increases the risk of injury to anyone inside. All affected vehicles are still at dealerships, so no owner notification letters are being mailed. Dealers will replace all four side door strikers and their attachment bolts, free of charge.

item.title: Chevrolet Colorado and GMC Canyon seat belt bolts loose
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Chevrolet Colorado and GMC Canyon trucks. On the left or right front seat, the bolt that holds the seat belt buckle to the vehicle may not have been tightened enough at the factory. A seat belt that is not held down tightly may not hold a person in place properly in a crash. Dealers will tighten the bolts on both front seat belt buckles.

item.title: Chevy Express and GMC Savana Cutaway Brake Line Risk
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Chevrolet Express Cutaway and GMC Savana Cutaway vehicles built with optional body mounts. On these vehicles, the brake line may not have enough clearance from the body mounts. Because of this, the brake line can rub against the body mount and become damaged over time, which can cause the brake line to leak brake fluid.

item.title: GM SUVs, Trucks Brake Warning Light May Fail
item.description: Certain Chevrolet, GMC, and Cadillac SUVs and trucks may have a software problem in the brake control module. This software is supposed to turn on a warning light when the brake fluid level gets too low, but it may fail to do so. Because of this, a driver might not realize the brake fluid is low, since the vehicle isn't giving them the warning it's designed to show.

item.title: Silverado trailer hitch bracket may let trailer detach
item.description: OEM Systems is recalling certain 2024 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 trucks. The rear bumper mounting bracket that the trailer hitch attaches to may not be strong enough for towing. This could allow a trailer being towed to detach from the vehicle.
